title: Align tenant header heuristics and stream handshake adapter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Normalize tenant discovery headers across streaming handshakes; add tolerant request-signature parsing to support legacy OpenAI-compat clients; improve streaming reconnect heuristics to preserve tool-call contexts.
description:
Context and motivation: customer support traces and internal canaries revealed intermittent auth failures for streaming tool-calls when requests cross tenant/org boundaries (hosted -> dedicated routing, or reverse proxied plugin gateways). Failures were caused by brittle header heuristics (we previously prioritized X-Project-Token prefixes only) and a mismatch between the OpenAI-compat streaming handshake and our session-anchored signed-nonce path. This PR unifies header heuristics and introduces a streaming handshake adapter to map legacy OpenAI compat frames to Redwood's tolerant auth checks.

Summary of changes: - Header normalizer: introduce x-rw-tenant and tenant discovery heuristics that try (in order) explicit x-rw-tenant, project-scoped token prefix, org-key fallback, and a safe header-mapping table populated for proxied requests. This is a best-effort discovery that does not change auth decision semantics (we still validate token scope/TTL) but reduces false negatives during routing. - Streaming handshake adapter: a small adapter layer that inspects the initial connect frame (OpenAI style "openai-session", or Redwood "rw-session-nonce") and normalizes fields into a canonical session object used by the runtime. Adapter tolerates both signed-nonce formats (v1 HMAC header and v2 structured signature) to maintain compatibility with older SDKs. - Signature parsing: make request-signature verification tolerant to 2 formats (X-RW-Signature: hmac={sig};v=1 and X-Signature: sig_v2={b64};alg=ed25519) and log a single metric for signature format fallbacks. - CORS: relax preflight mapping for streaming upgrade endpoints; the adapter now echoes project-origin hints in Access-Control-Allow-Headers if the request includes X-Project-Origin to avoid some browser preflight failures when proxying through third-party hubs. - Tool/function calling stability: preserve tool-call context across reconnects by applying a lightweight reconnect token derived from the original signed nonce (TTL 60s). If reconnect presents the reconnect token, adapter rehydrates the call context and hints to the tools-layer to resume safely. - Observability: add tenant_auth_attempts, tenant_auth_fallbacks, and stream_handshake_format metrics; wire them to the console dashboards.

Commits (high-level): - 4c2d9a2: header_normalizer: new package and heuristics implementation - b7f1e3d: stream handshake adapter and format toleration - d5a7b99: signature parsing helpers + metric emission - a2e8f12: unit + integration tests for streaming auth + reconnects - f9c4b01: docs and upgrade notes

Files changed (high-level): - internal/auth/header_normalizer.go: main heuristics + a small mapping table for proxied hosts - runtime/stream/handshake_adapter.go: adapter that canonicalizes session frames - api/openai_compat/stream_bridge.go: glue code for OpenAI compat clients - tests/integration/stream-auth-suite.test.js: end-to-end scenarios for reconnect and cross-tenant routing - docs/api/auth-header-mapping.md: explain the ordering and migration guidance - observability/metrics/tenant_auth_metrics.prom: metric names and labels - cmd/installer/upgrade-notes.md: operator guidance for private deployments

Small illustrative snippet (adapter canonicalization):

  // pseudo Go excerpt from handshake_adapter.go
  // prefer explicit tenant header, then token prefix, then org fallback
  tenant := header.Get("x-rw-tenant")
  if tenant == "" {
    tenant = headerNormalzer.MatchProjectPrefix(token)
  }

Review conversation (selected): - Liam Chen (reviewer): "Please ensure the tenant discovery ordering is documented and that falling back to org keys cannot grant higher privileges than the presented token scope." - Maya (author): "Documented ordering in docs/api/auth-header-mapping.md and enforced scope check in header_normalizer.MatchProjectPrefix; added unit tests to assert no privilege escalation." - Nora Gómez (reviewer): "The reconnect token TTL 60s seems short for some flaky networks; can we make it configurable via runtime flag?" - Maya: "Added runtime config flag stream.reconnect_token_ttl (default 60s) and an env override for Dedicated/Private installs; note in upgrade notes." - Evan Brooks (reviewer): "CI flaked on the integration suite once, but logs looked unrelated; please add a retry hook to the flaky external-hub test to reduce CI noise." - Maya: "Added a single-retry wrapper for the external-hub scenario and re-ran CI." - QA (comment): "Found an NPE on adapter when initial frame omitted an authorization header entirely; handling added and covered by tests."

CI summary: initial run (run #1) reported 1 failing test in tests/integration/stream-auth-suite.test.js (external-hub flake). After adding retry and handling empty auth-frame, rerun (run #2) passed all checks: unit, integration, lint, e2e-nightly. Metrics smoke test included.

Backward compatibility and migration notes: - This change is backward compatible: we accept both legacy and new signature formats and both openai-style and rw-style handshake frames. - Operators upgrading Dedicated/Private should review cmd/installer/upgrade-notes.md to optionally enable extended tenant-mapping lists for proxy gateways. - No breaking changes to public SDKs; we added a reconnect token path that SDKs can opt-into to improve resume behavior.

Why this is different from prior PRs: prior work focused on signed-nonce normalization and CORS mapping in isolation; this PR explicitly centralizes tenant discovery heuristics (to reduce cross-tenant false rejects) and introduces a streaming handshake adapter that acts as a single compatibility surface for both auth headers and streaming frame formats. It reduces duplication and clarifies where compatibility decisions live.

Testing performed: unit tests for header heuristics, property-based token-prefix parsing tests, integration suite exercising hosted->dedicated routing via a test proxy, manual canary on perf-canary with a small traffic slice verifying no latency regression, observability smoke tests verifying metric emission.

Merge details: squash merged by Maya Patel after approvals from Liam and Nora. Merge method: squash. Changelog: included in release notes for the next patch release.

Follow-ups / future work: - ENG-2145: expand tenant mapping ingestion from control plane for multi-tenant proxies - ENG-2212: plumb reconnect-token usage to TS/Go SDKs as an opt-in resume API - Add tracing spans to show which heuristic matched for easier debugging in the console
